title: Same-field concurrent offline edits can be silently overwritten (with a small POC comparing against a CRDT-style sync engine)
body:
Hi, I'm Mathéo. I'm 19 and I build offline-first software for places with unreliable connectivity, mostly [ZamSync](https://github.com/Etoile-Bleu/ZamSync), a sync engine for clinics in Bhutan that lose connectivity for days at a time and lose power mid-transfer. While looking into who else builds for that kind of environment, I found Primero. I wanted to see how the offline sync actually holds up under the conditions mine is built for, so instead of guessing I read the real code.

Two things I found, both checked against your actual source, not assumed.

**Same field, two offline devices.** The PATCH body is a genuine field-level diff (`record-form/utils.js`, `compactValues = (values, initialValues) => difference(values, initialValues)`), so two devices editing different fields on the same case already merge correctly. That part works well. But when two devices edit the *same* field while both offline, say two protection officers both updating `risk_level` on the same case without knowing about each other, neither the client queue nor the Rails update path (`children_controller`'s update action, `Child#update_properties`, `RecordMergeDataHashService.merge_data`) compares against the field's current value before writing. Whichever PATCH lands last just wins. The earlier value isn't gone from the database, `RecordHistory` still has it, but nothing merges it, flags it, or points anyone toward checking history for a silent overwrite.

**A connection that keeps failing.** `QUEUE_ALLOWED_RETRIES` is hardcoded to 3 in `queue/constants.js`. Once a queued item hits that ceiling it's dropped for good (`queue/index.js`, the `QUEUE_FAILED` handler). For a plain field edit, not an attachment, nothing tells the worker it happened, `onAttachmentError` only fires when `action.type` includes `"ATTACHMENT"`. A field worker whose connection just won't cooperate for a few days can lose an edit completely, no error, no trace anywhere.

title: Input and placeholder text contrast was too weak
body:
Problem: Default input/placeholder styling could fail AA readability.

Discovered: Automated scan color-contrast findings across admin forms.

How to replicate: Visit admin form pages, run axe color-contrast check on input text and placeholders.

body:

How to replicate: Open forms using text inputs, inspect rendered aria-label values in dev tools/accessibility tree.

Standards impacted: axe aria-prohibited-attr (as reported), WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value.

title: Login “Forgot password” was skipped in keyboard tab flow
body:
I wanted to explore this application and and its accessibility. I got it set up and just wanted to report a few issues.

Problem: The control behaved like a link button but was not consistently keyboard-focusable.

Discovered: Manual keyboard testing on login screen.

How to replicate: Open login page, use Tab from username/password/login; focus could skip the forgot-password control.

Standards impacted: WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard, WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order.

Upstream location: [upstream link component](https://github.com/primeroIMS/primero/blob/develop/app/javascript/components/action-button/components/link/component.jsx)
Your change: [fork commit e66900613f](https://github.com/mgifford/primero/commit/e66900613f#diff-d293fc6fca33da599c81d05579efacd4be51a0025733fa80e2cdf2298abee032R14-R19) and file [fork link component](https://github.com/mgifford/primero/blob/develop/app/javascript/components/action-button/components/link/component.jsx)

As you can see on the screen recording, I have identified a usability issue with the search functionality in the application: after clicking the search button, the search bar appears, but there is no back or close button available. I believe addressing this issue would significantly improve the user experience. As I am new to open source contributions, I would appreciate the opportunity to work on this easy fix.

title: Missing PRIMERO_MESSAGE_SECRET in local.env.sample.development
body:
PRIMERO_MESSAGE_SECRET is not set in local.env.sample.development file. 

Steps to reproduce

```
cd docker 
cp local.env.sample.development local.env
./build.sh all
./compose.local.sh up
```

Application does not run because in the script `check_required_variables` function of the `entrypoint.sh` of the docker/application/root  this variable is required.

Proposed solution:

Add PRIMERO_MESSAGE_SECRET to the example file.

title: Field Validation on the frontend
body:
On Primero 2.0 all the front end form fields are validated in the back end, after the save button is pressed and then the feedback/errors are populated at the bottom of the form. When the user has edited multiple forms, this poses an issue, as the errors for the prior forms get aggregated after validation, and get displayed at the bottom of the form the user is currently editing.

This problem can be alleviated by adding validation to some of the front-end fields. For instance, child's age bracket validation can be done on spot, it shouldn't have to be sent to the back-end for validation.

We would like to know if this is possible on V2, if so, what is the recommended method for adding those field validations, and where do we add them. Another thing we would like to know is how can we make the errors pop up immediately while the user is still in the relevant form. We would like to make these changes forward compatible as to not break the functionality when we inevitably migrate to a newer version, say 2.3.
